records.reason: Direct contemporaneous order from the media regulator; central evidence for state censorship.
Broad crackdown report with concrete arrest and blocking figures; strong corroboration of the 2022 repression pattern.
Same Memorial annual report as E0073 in another language/version; no separate evidentiary value.
Best Memorial summary of 2022 repression, with specific annual counts and categories of anti-war enforcement.
Strong synthesis of the Russian denial campaign immediately before invasion; direct and information-rich.
Direct check of Putin's own genocide claim in the invasion speech; useful as a specific false justification.
Another fact-check of Putin's war justifications; repeats the same speech-based falsity cluster without adding a material new fact.
Repackages Putin's self-defense claim already covered by stronger retained speech-based evidence.
Useful broad corroboration of the denial campaign, but it adds uncertainty about intent and overlaps with stronger retained items.
Corroborates the false-genocide rationale through ICJ-related reporting, but is secondary to the direct speech-based evidence.
Direct Putin statement that he had no choice; strong primary evidence for his public war justification.
Useful indirect wealth-network corroboration, but it is inferential and weaker than the documentary and official sanctions evidence.
Official sanctions action on Putin's daughters supports the family-wealth pattern, but it is still an enforcement notice rather than direct proof of hidden assets.
Another official sanctions notice on Putin-linked family members; repetitive once the official sanctions pattern is represented elsewhere.
Specific on Peskov family wealth and lifestyles, but still a proxy example rather than direct evidence about Putin himself.
Strong investigative synthesis of the Russian asset network; among the clearest broad wealth-pattern items.
Illustrative palace reporting, but ownership remains alleged and the item is weaker than the retained documentary and sanctions evidence.
High-quality synthesis of offshore-wealth networks, useful as background corroboration but not as direct as the retained incident-level items.
Useful network-pattern corroboration on offshore wealth, but largely overlaps with E0137 and the retained OCCRP material.
Specific documentary incident showing a Putin-linked villa funded through corporate spending; strong illustrative evidence.
Direct patronage example involving a long-time Putin associate receiving state benefit; useful evidence of elite favoritism.
Older but relevant pattern evidence on contract favoritism; helpful background, though less direct than the retained patronage items.
Direct documentary evidence of sanctions evasion planning by Putin associates; strong mechanism evidence.
Foundational official sanctions notice with unusually explicit claims about Putin's inner circle and financial links.
Useful confirmation that Navalny's prosecution was politically motivated, but it is narrower than the broader suppression evidence already retained.
Direct evidence of state suppression of Navalny's anti-corruption network; strong and specific.
Retrospective judicial record that corroborates the political-ends dispute, but it is procedural and less direct than the retained NGO evidence.

remaining_concerns: Much of the wealth and patronage material is inferential rather than direct proof of Putin's personal ownership or instruction.
Several war-justification items cluster around the same invasion speech and denial campaign, so the record is broad but not deeply independent on that mechanism.
A few of the strongest repression items are retrospective or advocacy-based rather than contemporaneous government records, which limits directness even when the pattern is clear.
